pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Who must do the burning when making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. Any learner
   B. An adult or the teacher
   C. The youngest learner
   D. Nobody

2. Percussion instruments make sound when they are (1 mark)
   A. struck, shaken or scraped
   B. sung into
   C. bowed with a stick of hair
   D. blown with air only

3. Which of these is a percussion instrument? (1 mark)
   A. Whistle
   B. Trumpet
   C. Drum
   D. Recorder

4. Which two positions are defenders that may enter the goal circle they defend? (1 mark)
   A. GS and C
   B. WA and C
   C. GD and GK
   D. WD and WA

5. A value scale strip shows (1 mark)
   A. only primary colours
   B. a picture of a mountain
   C. only black paint
   D. steps from light to dark of one colour

6. Dictation in music means (1 mark)
   A. singing louder
   B. drawing a picture
   C. copying a friend's book
   D. writing down a pattern you hear

7. Which of these four-beat patterns ends on a long note? (1 mark)
   A. ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te
   B. taa ta-te taa (rest)
   C. ta-te taa ta-te taa
   D. taa taa taa (rest)

8. Which is a quality of a good rhythmic pattern? (1 mark)
   A. Only one kind of note
   B. No beat
   C. Ending on a rest always
   D. Variation of note values

9. The sol-fa syllable r is pronounced (1 mark)
   A. rah
   B. ray
   C. roh
   D. ree

10. A slab of clay is (1 mark)
   A. a flat piece
   B. a thin roll
   C. a hollow cup
   D. a round ball

11. Which melody uses only steps? (1 mark)
   A. m d m d
   B. d r m r d
   C. d m d m
   D. d d m d

12. Which is a sprint distance in big athletics competitions? (1 mark)
   A. 100 metres
   B. 10 000 metres
   C. Marathon
   D. Half marathon

13. What happens on the command set? (1 mark)
   A. The runners run
   B. The runners raise their hips slightly and stay still
   C. The runners sit
   D. The race ends

14. Which should you remove before gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Your hair
   B. Your clothes
   C. Watches and bracelets
   D. Your smile

15. In a crab balance, your body is supported by (1 mark)
   A. the head only
   B. the back only
   C. the knees and elbows
   D. both hands and both feet

16. Pitch is (1 mark)
   A. the words
   B. how high or low a note is
   C. how loud it is
   D. how fast it is

17. The East African Community is (1 mark)
   A. a group of countries in East Africa that work together
   B. a school
   C. a river
   D. a type of drum

18. Singing softly at the end of a lullaby shows (1 mark)
   A. a loud dynamic
   B. a fast tempo
   C. a high pitch only
   D. a soft dynamic

19. The lens of a camera (1 mark)
   A. lets light in
   B. gives power
   C. keeps it cool
   D. stores photos

20. How should you hold a camera or tablet? (1 mark)
   A. Over your head
   B. By the lens
   C. By one corner
   D. With both hands

21. How should you clean the lens of a camera? (1 mark)
   A. With a soft, dry cloth
   B. With your fingers
   C. With a stick
   D. With water and sand

22. Another name for the descant recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. drum
   B. xylophone
   C. bass recorder
   D. soprano recorder

23. On the staff, the note A sits (1 mark)
   A. in the space between lines 2 and 3
   B. above the staff
   C. below the staff
   D. on line 1

24. A squeaky, very high sound usually means you are (1 mark)
   A. blowing too hard
   B. blowing too gently
   C. playing a drum
   D. holding it upside down

25. Why should you not use very hot water on a plastic recorder? (1 mark)
   A. It makes it louder
   B. It makes it heavier
   C. It makes it play higher
   D. It can bend the plastic

26. Why do we shower before entering the pool? (1 mark)
   A. To warm the water
   B. To learn to float
   C. To get dry
   D. To keep the pool clean

27. Which game uses small sinking toys? (1 mark)
   A. Circle walk
   B. Treasure hunt
   C. Follow the leader
   D. Water tag

28. The crab walk is done (1 mark)
   A. face down on the tummy
   B. standing tall
   C. on hands and feet with the tummy facing up
   D. lying still

29. Why do animal games often use singing or drumming? (1 mark)
   A. Rhythm helps players move together and adds fun
   B. To stop the game
   C. To scare animals
   D. To hide the players

30. Why are indigenous games part of our heritage? (1 mark)
   A. They have no meaning
   B. They were bought yesterday
   C. They come to us from earlier generations
   D. They are foreign

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Why should a short melody end on d? (2 marks)

32. Describe how to do the mushroom float. (3 marks)

33. Why should you collect only dead or fallen twigs for charcoal? (2 marks)

34. Describe the steps of a glide. (4 marks)

35. Describe how to make a portfolio from manila paper. (5 marks)

36. Describe the steps of modelling the letters d, r and m on clay slabs. (5 marks)

37. Describe how to make a montage on ball games. (4 marks)

38. Describe how to compose, write and perform an original four-beat rhythmic pattern. (5 marks)

39. Give four hygiene measures for using a recorder. (4 marks)

40. What is the East African Community? (3 marks)

41. Describe how to present an artwork from your portfolio. (4 marks)

42. Name any two players' positions in netball. (2 marks)

43. Give three qualities of a neat montage. (3 marks)

44. Describe how to draw a drum with tonal value using the smudge technique. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — An adult or the teacher
   Fire is dangerous, so only an adult does the burning.

2. A — struck, shaken or scraped
   A percussion instrument is played by hitting, shaking or scraping it.

3. C — Drum
   A drum is struck to make sound. The others are played by blowing.

4. C — GD and GK
   The Goal Defence and the Goal Keeper may play in their defending circle.

5. D — steps from light to dark of one colour
   A scale strip shows one colour changing from light to dark.

6. D — writing down a pattern you hear
   In dictation, the teacher plays or claps and you write it.

7. C — ta-te taa ta-te taa
   Only the first ends on a crotchet (taa).

8. D — Variation of note values
   Good patterns vary the note values.

9. B — ray
   The syllable r is ray.

10. A — a flat piece
   A slab is a flat sheet of clay.

11. B — d r m r d
   Each move in d r m r d is to a neighbouring note.

12. A — 100 metres
   The sprints are 100 m, 200 m and 400 m.

13. B — The runners raise their hips slightly and stay still
   On set, runners lift the hips and hold still.

14. C — Watches and bracelets
   Jewellery can hurt you or others.

15. D — both hands and both feet
   A crab balance rests on two hands and two feet.

16. B — how high or low a note is
   Accurate pitch means singing the right notes.

17. A — a group of countries in East Africa that work together
   The community brings countries together to cooperate.

18. D — a soft dynamic
   Softness is dynamics.

19. A — lets light in
   The lens gathers light for the picture.

20. D — With both hands
   Two hands prevent dropping.

21. A — With a soft, dry cloth
   A soft cloth cleans without scratching.

22. D — soprano recorder
   The descant is the soprano recorder.

23. A — in the space between lines 2 and 3
   A is in the space between G and B.

24. A — blowing too hard
   Gentle air makes a good tone.

25. D — It can bend the plastic
   Heat can warp plastic.

26. D — To keep the pool clean
   It removes dirt and sweat.

27. B — Treasure hunt
   Players pick up toys from the pool bottom.

28. C — on hands and feet with the tummy facing up
   It is like the crab balance, but moving.

29. A — Rhythm helps players move together and adds fun
   Music sets the pace.

30. C — They come to us from earlier generations
   Heritage is what we inherit.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: d is the home note. Ending on it makes the melody sound finished.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each idea.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: In shallow water take a breath and put the face in. Bend the knees and hug them to the chest with the chin tucked. The back rises to the surface. Hold for a few seconds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: To protect the environment and living trees. Dead twigs are also dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for protecting living trees, 1 mark for the environment or dry wood.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stand with the back to the wall and arms stretched overhead. Put the feet on the wall and bend the knees. Take a breath and put the face in. Push off gently with the body straight.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Fold two large pieces of manila paper to make a folder and trim the edges. Punch holes and add a string tie. Paste coloured paper or fabric on the cover. Write a label with name and class. Put in the works with dates and notes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the five parts.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Prepare and knead clay. Roll a slab and cut three rectangles of different sizes. Make coils. Shape a coil into each letter and scratch and wet where they join. Press on gently, smooth, and let dry slowly in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for preparing clay, cutting slabs, making coils, joining, and drying.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Collect and cut pictures of ball games from old papers. Arrange them on a background without gluing, overlapping the pieces. Paste the back ones first and then the others. Add a title and let it dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose four beats. Fill each with a crotchet, a pair of quavers or a rest. Make sure the pattern has variation and ends on a crotchet. Write it with rhythm names and note symbols. Clap it to a steady beat and improve it after feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for choosing beats, using different values, ending on a long note, writing it and performing it.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands before playing; do not share it without cleaning; do not eat while playing; wipe the mouthpiece; clean it properly. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: A group of countries in East Africa that work together on matters such as trade, travel and peace.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for group of countries, 1 mark for East Africa, 1 mark for working together.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold it carefully, say the title, explain the materials and skills, tell the message, say what you like and what you would change, and listen to feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Goal Shooter, Goal Attack, Wing Attack, Centre, Wing Defence, Goal Defence, Goal Keeper. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clean cut edges, no glue marks, well-overlapped pieces, firmly stuck and a clear title. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the outline lightly. Shade the dark parts by pressing harder and the light parts by pressing lightly. Rub the shading with a finger or tissue to blend. Leave the brightest part white.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.
